functionalObligations.text: a depositor brings a stablecoin, without identity checks or accreditation, and receives a transferable token representing the deposit
functionalObligations.note: SCOPE DECISION, stated explicitly as stage 1 requires. Obligations F1-F11 decompose HUMA 2.0, the permissionless Solana product launched April 2025, which carries 100% of the $219,355,660.45 that ranks this application. Obligations F12-F24 decompose HUMA INSTITUTIONAL, the permissioned tranched product the corpus's element set actually describes; each is marked. The two must not be conflated: decomposing both under one name produces a construction that reproduces neither. CORRECTION to the corpus: Aw is REFUTED for the TVL-carrying entity — Huma 2.0 is open to all. EPISTEMIC LABEL for F1-F11: the Solana program HumaXepHnjaRCpjYTokxY4UtaJcmx41prQ8cxGmFC5fn is closed-source, absent from the 00labs org, and returns is_verified false from the Solana verified-builds registry, so every obligation here rests on documentation and audit scopes rather than on readable source.

functionalObligations.text: the default claim class pays an administered eight per cent annual rate, stated as subject to monthly adjustment at the issuer's discretion
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. The same administered-rate object as the Sky Savings Rate, appearing independently at a second protocol in this lane: no utilisation curve, no auction, no market. DEPARTURE: the corpus emits Ix for Huma and stage 1 records no evidence of index accrual on either product — the EVM path computes and PAYS OUT yield at epoch close (processYieldForLenders then payoutYield) rather than accruing it into a share price, and the Solana accrual form is unverifiable because the program is closed. Ix is therefore dropped rather than assumed.

functionalObligations.text: the holder may switch instantly, for gas only, to a second claim class that pays no cash yield at all
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. A claim class whose holder ELECTS between a cash yield and a non-cash reward stream, switchable at will, has no symbol. Convex's cvxCRV reward-ratio election is the same shape in a different setting.

functionalObligations.text: in exchange the zero-yield class maximises an off-chain point balance which is the holder's entire return
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. Em requires protocol-funded emissions of a token; points are an off-chain ledger of a future discretionary claim. The same object appears at Pendle, which taxes third-party points at 5%.

functionalObligations.text: a depositor may optionally commit for three or six months to multiply that point rate; commitments can be lengthened but never shortened, and breaking one retroactively forfeits the bonus, including on transfer
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. The lockup does not change the yield, the claim's seniority or its redemption terms — its only consequence is a discretionary multiplier on a non-token reward. Nothing in the vocabulary names a commitment with no claim-side effect.

functionalObligations.text: redemption requests are batched and settled by a scheduled off-chain job in an all-or-nothing manner
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. APPROXIMATE: Wq names the deferred exit, not the all-or-nothing settlement rule.

functionalObligations.text: redemption is first-come-first-served against a global daily cap that resets at midnight UTC, and requests above the cap are rejected outright rather than queued, against a documented service level of one to seven days
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. Wq names a queue that preserves order across time; this is a RATIONING RULE that discards excess demand at a period boundary, plus a promise that appears in no contract.

functionalObligations.text: a holder may bypass the redemption path entirely by selling the claim token into third-party automated market makers
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. The real exit liquidity for the ranked entity is supplied by protocols outside it, and the vocabulary again has no way to mark an element as inherited from a dependency. Same defect as Spark/Ps and CIAN/Ct.

functionalObligations.text: the yield paid to depositors originates in transaction fees from businesses using an accelerated cross-border payment rail, in practice short-duration advances originated by a single named counterparty
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. No element for the SOURCE of yield, and none for originator concentration: the borrower on the deployed EVM pools is named in the deployment itself (Arf). A protocol can be fully expressible in this vocabulary while its solvency argument is entirely invisible.

functionalObligations.text: the deposits fund advances that are not secured by on-chain collateral
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. Documentary only: the program is closed-source and not a verified build, so this cannot be checked against code for the entity carrying the TVL. Stage 3 should note that emitting Uc here arms L3 (Uc implies Aw + At + (Bs|Tr) + obligor) against a product that has none of Aw, At or Tr — see F21.

functionalObligations.text: the redemption round and the price refresh happen only because scheduled off-chain jobs run and call them
functionalObligations.note: HUMA 2.0. RESIDUE. Ep names a period boundary; nothing names that the boundary exists only if someone calls it. Third instance of the keeper-liveness gap in this lane, after CIAN's three-day NAV revert and Convex's paid harvest bounty.

functionalObligations.text: a lender passes identity and accreditation checks and is approved by a designated operator before being allowed to deposit
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. This is where the corpus's Aw belongs; it does not apply to the ranked entity.

functionalObligations.text: deposits go into a senior or a junior claim with declared seniority on loss and a fixed or risk-adjusted split of yield between them
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only.

functionalObligations.text: the senior claim may not exceed four times the junior claim, enforced on deposit and again in the ordering of redemptions
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. RESIDUE, upgraded from a corpus observation to a verified constant: lpConfig.maxSeniorJuniorRatio = 4. Tr names the waterfall, not the thickness constraint that makes it safe. It is also the magnitude cap (slot 3) on the mandate in F17-F20.

functionalObligations.text: a first-loss cover funded by borrowers, insurers and administrators absorbs a default ahead of the junior claim, up to the lesser of a cap and a rate applied to the default amount, and its capital is deliberately left undeployed
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. APPROXIMATE, corpus marker retained: this is genuinely first-loss capital but it is not slashed by a protocol rule, it simply sits lower in the waterfall. Tr and Bs overlap here and the vocabulary gives no guidance on which to prefer.

functionalObligations.text: all administrative fees are automatically routed into that cover until it reaches its maximum
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd), a DEPARTURE the corpus does not carry: realised fees are recycled into the backstop rather than paid out, which is a distribution with a named non-obvious recipient.

functionalObligations.text: one stored address is the only caller permitted to approve a borrower into the pool
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent), partial fit — Aw names the enumeration (_onlyEvaluationAgent), not the authority. The address is a single field, address public evaluationAgent, set by the pool owner or the protocol owner.

functionalObligations.text: that address alone declares a borrower in default, and the loss it declares flows directly into the seniority waterfall
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Sv), promoted from a corpus marker into the construction and the single best fit for this candidate in the lane. triggerDefault(address) is _onlyEvaluationAgent and returns (principalLoss, yieldLoss, feesLoss) straight into the waterfall. This is servicing and determination discretion in its intended sense, and it satisfies L6.

functionalObligations.text: the same address alone sets the borrower's credit limit and the yield in basis points, and may revise both afterwards by raising the limit, changing the yield, extending the term or waiving a late fee
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. RESIDUE, and the precise boundary of the lane's best-fitting candidate: Sv names the authority to DETERMINE AN OUTCOME on a claim; it does not name the authority to SET THE PRICE or SIZE THE EXPOSURE. Those are allocation acts and they are unnamed. Also unnamed: Aw is a static admission test, and approveBorrower opens a continuing relationship that is repriced and resized over time.

functionalObligations.text: that address is required to hold junior-tranche capital in the very pool whose credit it underwrites, checked as a liquidity requirement
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. RESIDUE, and unique in this lane: slot 7 of the mandate shape, skin in the game. _checkLiquidityRequirementForEA makes Huma the only protocol here whose discretionary agent is capitalised against its own decisions. Bs names slashable first-loss capital but not capital posted as a CONDITION OF HOLDING AN AUTHORITY.

functionalObligations.text: the financed obligation is minted as a non-fungible token recording an amount, a currency code, a creation date, a maturity date, a paid amount and a creator, by whoever holds the minting role
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. RESIDUE, and sharper than the corpus's version. The struct stores NO PAYER, no document hash, no jurisdiction and no verification of any kind; the only link to the world is a hash of the originator's own internal reference and an opaque uri. So the receivable is an on-chain object but an ASSERTION, not evidence. DEPARTURE: the corpus emits At as the closest available symbol. At is REFUTED, not merely approximate — L27 requires a named attester, independence, a stated assurance level, a staleness bound and recourse, and none exists, so At cannot be discharged at all. Dropping At will make L3 fail in stage 3 for the Uc emitted at F10 and F22; that failure IS the finding, and X11b (Uc with all of them and weak underwriting, class H) should be considered for arming. No element for off-chain legal recourse either: nothing in the contracts references a jurisdiction, a governing agreement or a servicer of record, yet that is what makes the pool solvent.

functionalObligations.text: a borrower draws against a revolving line, a receivable-backed line at an advance rate below one hundred per cent, or an outright purchase of the receivable, each with a due date and a period count
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. Ft is APPROXIMATE and its scope must be stated: it names the BORROWER-side dated obligation, not the investor claim, which is open-ended with epoch redemption. Stage 1 records that Ft is doubly wrong for Huma 2.0, where the investor holds a perpetual token whose optional lockup dates nothing.

functionalObligations.text: redemption requests are batched to a period aligned with the pool's payment cycle, senior filled first, shortfalls pro-rated, the unfilled portion rolled to the next period, and the proceeds claimed by a separate call
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. Senior is filled first specifically to avoid breaching the 4:1 ratio of F14, so the ordering is a solvency device rather than a fairness rule — which Wq does not name. The concrete epoch length is UNKNOWN.

functionalObligations.text: designated pausers can stop all outbound movement of money, and only the protocol owner can restart it
functionalObligations.note: HUMA INSTITUTIONAL only. MANDATE SLOT 5 (halt). DEPARTURE: the corpus carries no control-plane element for Huma. Gp does not express that the right to stop and the right to restart are deliberately held by different parties — the same split Sky builds explicitly with grantors and revokers. Stage 1 also records a ninth role that exists only in code, a Sentinel service account (onlyPoolOwnerOrSentinelServiceAccount), which is the on-chain identity of the automation in F11.

paper.title: Huma Finance V2
paper.label: cat:yld:huma
paper.blurb: A depositor brings a stablecoin and receives a transferable token in one of two classes: a class paying an administered rate that the issuer states is subject to revision at its discretion, or a class paying no cash yield whatever and maximising an off-chain point balance instead. The holder switches between them instantly, for the cost of gas. The yield originates in transaction fees paid by businesses using an accelerated cross-border payment rail --- in practice short-duration advances to a single named counterparty --- and alongside this runs a permissioned product with the tranched architecture, where approved lenders take a senior or a junior claim, borrowers draw against a revolving line, a receivable-backed line or an outright purchase of the receivable, and one address alone sets the credit limit, sets the rate and declares default. Exit from the retail claim is first-come-first-served against a global daily cap that resets at midnight, with requests above the cap rejected outright rather than queued; exit from the tranched product is an epoch batch, senior filled first and shortfalls pro-rated into the next round. A holder who will not wait sells the claim into a third-party market maker.
paper.witnessReason: The witness adds a servicing discretion, a guardian and fee distribution, and drops the attestation and the accrual index. Servicing is a candidate element of the vocabulary and it fits exactly one act here, that a single address declares a borrower in default and the loss it declares flows straight into the seniority waterfall; the index goes because neither claim moves by one, the retail return being a stated rate and a point balance. The attestation goes because there is none to name: the financed obligation is minted by whoever holds the minting role, recording an amount, a currency code, a creation date and a maturity date, with no payer, no document hash, no jurisdiction and no attester --- so among the alternatives the undercollateralised-credit term leaves open there is none the code supports, the term stays open, the construction is rejected and a prohibition arms. The larger departure is which product is being decomposed: the element-set decomposition describes the permissioned tranched pools, whose code is open and frozen, while every unit of the capital sits in a permissionless retail product on another chain whose program is closed-source and returns unverified from the verified-builds registry, so the witness carries both and says which obligations belong to which.
paper.residueNote: The rejection is not a defect in the witness. The requirement tables ask for an attestation behind undercollateralised credit and this protocol has none, so the term stays open and the verdict states precisely what is true of it --- and the residue then says why that matters, because the financed obligation is an assertion by its own minter and the solvency of the pool rests on agreements in a legal system the code cannot reference. On the other side of the same protocol the category's mandate appears again, one step further than elsewhere: the address that determines an outcome on a claim also sets the \emph{price} of the credit and sizes the exposure, and of those three powers only the first is named. It is also the only agent in this category required to hold capital in the very pool whose credit it underwrites, and the vocabulary cannot record that either, so the one instance where the discretion is bonded reads the same as the instances where it is not. What is left is a retail claim whose holder elects between cash and points, and a redemption rule that is a rationing cap plus a promise made outside every contract.
